features: **Error tracking, with bug reports emailed to support.** Every server error, failed background job, script error in someone's browser and failing health check becomes an Issue under Administration → Error tracking — grouped, so a bug hit a thousand times is one Issue — and the team is told when it is new, comes back, or spreads. Alerts can go by email, Telegram, Viber, a signed webhook, or a ticket in Jira, ServiceNow, Zendesk and other help desks.

**Bug emails in the support format:** the subject names the company, the environment and the problem (`[Company A · Production] …`), followed by Description, What, When, Where, Who, the raw log (with addresses, tokens and long numbers masked), a recommended fix, and whether downtime is needed.
**A "Vendor support" alert channel to support@isnek.com is set up on upgrade.** It is visible and can be switched off under Error tracking → Alert channels.

**Menu links that refuse their own user are now reported.** If someone's menu offers a page and the page answers "403 Forbidden", that is an Issue — the kind of bug that crashes nothing and so was previously only found when someone complained.
actions: **Error reports are emailed to support@isnek.com by default.** If they must not leave your network, add `DJANGO_SUPPORT_ALERT_EMAIL=` (empty) to `.env` **before** running the update; afterwards, switch the "Vendor support" channel off under Error tracking → Alert channels.

**Alerts need working email delivery** (Administration → Email delivery) and the **Site address**, for the "Open the issue" button. Set the **Company name** under Branding and the environment (Production / Staging) under System settings, so the subject says whose server sent it.
`./update.sh v2.17.0` applies everything, including the refreshed nginx configuration. No downtime beyond the usual restart.
fixes: **GRC Administrators signed in through SSO can open Users and Groups.** Both pages answered 403 because the Administrator profile lacked the permissions those pages check. Administrators can now view, add and change accounts and groups. A break-glass superuser account can be seen but not changed by anyone who is not a superuser, so it cannot be taken over.

**Every access profile is now checked against its table automatically:** a test signs in as each of the six profiles and confirms each row of Administration → Access profiles against the real pages, and opens every menu link each profile is shown.
**Pages load their stylesheets and scripts faster:** static files are compressed and cached for an hour.
